speaker: presidenta
text: Good afternoon, the Vice-President and I welcome you to our press conference.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I would like to thank President Nagel for his kind hospitality and express our special gratitude to his staff for the excellent organisation of today’s meeting of the Governing Council.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The conflict in the Middle East continues to generate inflation pressures, and inflation is set to remain well above target for an extended period.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Today’s decision underscores our commitment to setting monetary policy to ensure that inflation stabilises at our two per cent target in the medium term.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The baseline of the new ECB staff projections sees headline inflation averaging 3.0 per cent in 2026, 2.5 per cent in 2027 and 2.1 per cent in 2028.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: For inflation excluding energy and food, the baseline foresees 2.5 per cent in 2026, 2.6 per cent in 2027 and 2.3 per cent in 2028.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Compared with June, the baseline projection for inflation in 2026 is unchanged, while it has been revised up for 2027 and 2028.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The baseline projection for economic growth is 0.9 per cent for 2026, 1.4 per cent for 2027 and 1.5 per cent for 2028.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This is an upward revision for both 2026 and 2027, mainly reflecting the greater than expected resilience of the euro area economy.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The outlook remains highly uncertain, with risks to the upside for inflation and to the downside for economic growth.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In relation to the energy shock, the updated scenarios put together by staff illustrate the broad range of outcomes for how growth and inflation would evolve under different assumptions about its intensity and duration, as well as its indirect and second-round effects.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: With today’s decision, we remain well positioned to navigate the uncertainty caused by the conflict.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We will follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In particular, our interest rate decisions will be based on our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it, in light of the incoming economic and financial data, as well as the dynamics of underlying inflation and the strength of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are not pre-committing to a particular rate path.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The decisions taken today are set out in a press release available on our website.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I will now outline in more detail how we see the economy and inflation developing and will then explain our assessment of financial and monetary conditions.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The economy proved resilient in the second quarter, despite headwinds from the energy shock.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Growth was broad-based across countries and sectors.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This pattern is likely to have continued into the third quarter.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Manufacturing continues to perform solidly as governments spend more on defence and infrastructure.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Consumer confidence has rebounded from low levels, helping services recover from the initial energy shock.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Increased AI-related activity is visible in digital services, business investment and exports.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The labour market has remained robust, with the unemployment rate unchanged in July at 6.4 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Growth in employment and the labour force continues to slow, while productivity has gradually picked up.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Looking ahead, the near-term growth outlook has improved compared with the last round of staff projections, reflecting, in particular, the resilience of private consumption and public spending.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Over the medium term, consumption should be supported by gradually falling energy prices and a strong labour market.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: Growth will increasingly be bolstered by business and housing investment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Export growth should benefit from rising foreign demand but is being held back by competitiveness challenges and uncertainty about global trade policies.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Higher potential growth requires structural reform and has to be underpinned by sound public finances.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Simplifying and harmonising rules across the EU’s Single Market, accelerating the energy transition and completing the savings and investments union are key building blocks.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: As the process for agreeing on the legal framework for the digital euro moves into its final stage, we reiterate the importance of reaching agreement on the Single Currency package as quickly as possible.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Fiscal responses to the energy shock should be temporary, targeted and tailored.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation increased to 3.3 per cent in August, from 2.9 per cent in July.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Energy price inflation rose to 14.3 per cent, after 10.3 per cent in July.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: This increase is likely to reflect, in particular, a strong contribution from refining margins on liquid fuels, as well as higher energy commodity prices.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Food price inflation remained unchanged at 1.2 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation excluding energy and food edged down to 2.4 per cent, from 2.5 per cent in July, with goods inflation increasing from 0.9 per cent to 1.2 per cent and services inflation falling from 3.3 per cent to 3.0 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Most measures of underlying inflation were broadly stable in July.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Wages do not show a material response to the energy shock at this stage.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Compensation per employee grew at an annual rate of 3.3 per cent in the second quarter, down from 3.5 per cent in the first quarter.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Rising labour productivity has also helped contain growth in unit labour costs, which slowed to 2.6 per cent, from 3.5 per cent in the first quarter.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: At the same time, growth in unit profits rose from 0.3 per cent to 2.2 per cent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Looking ahead, the ECB’s wage tracker points to a modest uptick, to 2.7 per cent, in negotiated wage growth in the first half of 2027.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Inflation expectations over shorter horizons remain at elevated levels, but most measures of longer-term inflation expectations stand at around 2 per cent, supporting the stabilisation of inflation around target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The conflict in the Middle East and recent developments in Russia’s unjustified war against Ukraine have pushed the path of energy prices up further.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This is likely to keep headline inflation well above target into the first half of 2027.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Thereafter, energy inflation should decline and turn negative up to mid-2028, bringing headline inflation down.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Higher energy prices are expected to feed through gradually to core and food price inflation.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The improved economic outlook should also contribute to slightly higher core inflation, which is expected to keep rising until early 2027 and stay elevated for the rest of the year, before moderating in 2028.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Overall, headline inflation is expected to return to around target towards the end of 2027, supported by the effects of higher interest rates.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: We will continue to monitor closely the size and persistence of the energy price increase and how it feeds through to price and wage-setting, inflation expectations and overall economic dynamics.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: This is due, in particular, to the Middle East conflict and developments in Russia’s unjustified war against Ukraine.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Renewed disruption of energy supplies could cause energy prices to rise further and for longer than currently expected.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: This would weigh on real incomes, spending and investment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: A worsening of global financial market sentiment or spillovers in global bond markets could tighten credit conditions and thereby dampen demand.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: A resurgence of trade tensions between major economies could also further disrupt supply chains, reduce exports and weaken consumption and investment.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: By contrast, growth could turn out to be higher if the economy and energy markets were to adapt more quickly than expected to the disruption caused by the ongoing conflicts or if these were resolved sustainably.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Moreover, the adoption of new technologies by euro area firms and spending on defence and infrastructure, as well as reforms to enhance productivity and complete the EU’s Single Market, may drive up growth by more than expected.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: This is due, in particular, to the Middle East conflict and developments in Russia’s unjustified war against Ukraine.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The energy shock could intensify further and its effects on other prices and wages could be stronger than currently expected.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Gas prices, in particular, could increase in the event of further supply disruptions or an unusually cold winter coinciding with low storage levels.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The longer energy prices stay high, the more likely they are to drive up broader inflation through indirect and second-round effects.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: Renewed trade tensions could give rise to more fragmented global supply chains, curtail the supply of critical raw materials and worsen capacity constraints in the euro area economy.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Extreme weather events, potentially reinforced by intensifying “El Niño” conditions, and the unfolding climate and nature crises more broadly, could drive up food prices by more than expected.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: By contrast, inflation could turn out to be lower if ongoing geopolitical conflicts were resolved sustainably or if indirect or second-round effects from the recent energy price shock proved less pronounced than anticipated.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: More volatile and risk-averse financial markets could weigh on demand and thereby lower inflation as well.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: Market interest rates have increased since our previous meeting, reflecting similar moves in global markets.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Following our interest rate increase in June, bank lending rates for firms have risen, to stand at 3.8 per cent in June and July, from 3.6 per cent in May.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: The cost of market-based corporate debt stood at 4.0 per cent in July, which was similar to previous months and well above its level before the conflict in the Middle East.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The annual growth rate of bank lending to firms, which usually responds to changes in monetary policy with a longer delay, increased further to 4.4 per cent in July, from 4.0 per cent in May and June.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The annual growth rate of corporate bond issuance was 3.4 per cent, after 3.6 per cent in June and 3.3 per cent in May.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Mortgage rates were unchanged in June and July, at 3.5 per cent, while mortgage lending growth softened to 3.0 per cent in July, from 3.1 per cent in May and June.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: The Governing Council today decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: We are committed to setting monetary policy to ensure that inflation stabilises at our two per cent target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We will follow a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach to determining the appropriate monetary policy stance.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Our interest rate decisions will be based on our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it, in light of the incoming economic and financial data, as well as the dynamics of underlying inflation and the strength of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are not pre-committing to a particular rate path.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: In any case, we stand ready to adjust all of our instruments within our mandate to ensure that inflation stabilises sustainably at our medium-term target and to preserve the smooth functioning of monetary policy transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are now ready to take your questions.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You give me a chance to, yet again, give what I like most, which is framework guidance.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And that framework guidance is really encapsulated in the three key pillars that we use: the inflation outlook with the assessment of the risk, the underlying inflation, and the transmission.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Those are the three pillars.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And of course we do that on the basis of the analysis of the shock, in the present circumstances predominantly a supply shock, of which we analyse the intensity, the duration and the propagation.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We do that on a meeting-by-meeting basis, and we are data-dependent.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You've heard me say that probably ad nauseum to your taste, but this is what we stick to and this is how we operate.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Now, markets do what they have to do, and we do what we have to do, which is to provide price stability, which has been defined, as you know, as the 2% target in the medium term.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: When I talk about framework guidance, this is what I'm talking about, and I'm assuming that markets find it helpful, in order to determine the path, that they understand it.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But they do their job.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We do our job.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And I can assure you that the entire discussions that we had today were focused on today's decision.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We have not actually debated at all any kind of future path, the likelihood of this or the likelihood of that, because we are dead serious about the framework that we observe and that we want to collectively respect.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I will say this: When there is something to report about me personally, you'll be the first one to know.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: After my grandchildren.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And there is nothing to report.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You might try multiple angles to get me to identify what is the next move, but this is really not the point.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And I can assure you that we are not taking a view as to which direction we go at our next meeting.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And why is that?
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I'll come back to the neutral rate in a second.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You have a second question.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Why don't you give it to me at the same time?
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Then it's fair for the others because they have to put their questions at the same time.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I'll go back to the answer I was giving you for your first question.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We don't focus on the meeting and on the data to annoy either you or the observers or the analysts.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We do it because we are in this uncertainty that can change things almost overnight.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I'll give you an example: Refining margins.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: If I had talked to you about refining margins six months ago, we wouldn't have known what we are really talking about.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Now, whether you call it the crack spread or the refining margin, on liquid fuel, now we all know what it's about.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And we all know that diesel is used by a category of economic actors.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And we know now that it's yet another bottleneck.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Those things happen as a result of multiple geopolitical changes, as a result of supply chain reorganinations, as a result of adjustment of the economy.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And because we have that level of uncertainty, we simply cannot anticipate what exactly will be the next move.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Now, you could argue that, in the present state and assuming that nothing changes, we should be doing this and that, but this is not how we are trying to address the issue of price stability.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We are focusing on what the data deliver today and we are ready to demonstrate the appropriate agility in whichever direction it is needed.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I hope I'm clear on that.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Second point that you raised is the issue of the upper end of the neutral rate band.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: This neutral rate band is a work in progress on a constant basis.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It is produced by staff, as you know, and they have delivered a band that they consider as the neutral rate band.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But this is highly conceptua.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You cannot actually pinpoint the neutral rate, because it's a factor of multiple variables that change over time, and because it is supposed to be defined in times of no shock.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And we are constantly under shocks.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So, we are not attaching great importance in the current circumstances to the neutral rate.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And your second question -- I don't want to leave you frustrated because I did not address your question.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: You say that our projections are not at target.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So, the decision that we took today – which was, by the way, a unanimous decision,– was a no-brainer.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: What we will have to do in the future will be determined at each and every meeting.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But what I can tell you, and this is in the monetary policy statement, is that we are determined to deliver on our target.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Voilà.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: On bond yields: It's a phenomenon, as we indicated clearly in the monetary policy statement, which is taking place across global markets.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It's not a euro-specific issue.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: It's happening across the world.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And it's a factor having multiple causes.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: I would mention, as the obvious one, supply and demand.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: When you have significant financing needs arising out of -- I will not say hyperscalers, because I think that is actually narrowing the economic sector that is concerned -- any AI-related activity at the moment is a potential consumer of financing.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And whatever form it takes: it used to be restricted to equity, it's moving now clearly to bonds, in the private credit area as well.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So that's a key driver of what we see.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: And then there are fundamentals having to do with each and every economy, and I would venture that the US market, which is so large and so liquid andsuch a driver, is also playing a role.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Having said all that, it's incorporated in our projections, taken into account, and obviously we are monitoring attentively what is happening in the markets and particularly on the long end of the yield curve.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: On inflation: Thank you for asking that question because it gives me a chance to really explain what we discussed over the meeting and how we see things.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: We have been, in a way, surprised at both ends, and that's the reason why we have revised upward our projection for growth, as well as for inflation, although at different horizons.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: We have been surprised by the resilience of our economy and we had anticipated in previous projections that growth would be lower than what we are seeing and what we are projecting.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So we moved from 0.8% to 0.9% for 2026.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: If you factor into that numbers released post cut-off date, it's actually more than 0.9%.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: Q2 was 0.6%, it came as an upward surprise.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: If you factor that number into the projection – but it's not a projection, because the cut-off date was earlier – but if you were to revise it, it's more than 0.9%.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So we've been surprised in a way for good, because growth is stronger than we had anticipated, the economy is adjusting better.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: And we've also been surprised on the inflation front, because we have seen inflation, in a way, lower than we had anticipated.
label: dovish

speaker: presidenta
text: This is particularly the case for food.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: But we believe that inflation will be longer lasting than we had anticipated.
label: hawkish

speaker: presidenta
text: So you have these two phenomena: More resilience, better adjustment of the economy, lower inflation, but longer lasting.
label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: So we are adjusting our projections on that basis.
label: neutral

label: neutral

speaker: presidenta
text: TSo, there are multiple reasons why the digital euro is important.
label: neutral

text: That's number one.

label: neutral
